graph.title: Purchase-to-Pay (Demo)
graph.summary: Requisition through to payment, with key approval, validation, and three-way-match controls.

nodes.label: Need identified
nodes.source: The process kicks off when a department requester raises a purchase requisition

nodes.label: Raise purchase requisition
nodes.description: Requester enters vendor, line items, quantities and cost centre in the ERP.
nodes.source: The requester fills in the vendor, line items, quantities and cost centre.

nodes.label: Approve requisition
nodes.description: Manager reviews requisition against department budget.
nodes.source: The manager reviews the requisition against the department budget.

nodes.label: Approved?
nodes.source: If the manager rejects it, the requisition goes back to the requester to amend or cancel. If approved, it moves on.

nodes.label: Amend or cancel
nodes.source: the requisition goes back to the requester to amend or cancel

nodes.label: Create & issue PO
nodes.description: Procurement converts the requisition into a purchase order and sends it to the vendor.
nodes.source: the procurement team converts the requisition into a purchase order and issues it to the vendor

nodes.label: PO value check
nodes.description: System verifies PO value is within the approved requisition amount before dispatch.
nodes.source: The system automatically checks that the PO value is within the approved requisition amount before it can be dispatched

nodes.label: Record goods receipt
nodes.description: Receiving team records goods receipt in the ERP on delivery.
nodes.source: the receiving team records a goods receipt in the ERP

nodes.label: Three-way match
nodes.description: AP clerk matches purchase order, goods receipt and invoice.

control.riskAddressed: Paying for goods not received or at the wrong price

nodes.source: an AP clerk performs a three-way match between the purchase order, the goods receipt and the invoice

nodes.label: Match OK?
nodes.source: If the three-way match fails, the invoice is parked and sent to procurement to investigate the discrepancy.

nodes.label: Park & investigate
nodes.description: Discrepant invoice is parked and sent to procurement to investigate.
nodes.source: the invoice is parked and sent to procurement to investigate the discrepancy

nodes.label: Post invoice for payment
nodes.source: If it matches, the AP clerk posts the invoice for payment.

nodes.label: Weekly payment run
nodes.description: Payments team settles the invoice in the scheduled run.
nodes.source: the payments team runs the weekly payment run to settle the invoice

openPoints.issue: The walkthrough doesn't say who approves the weekly payment run or how the payment file is checked before release.
openPoints.question: Who reviews and approves the payment run before funds are released, and what evidence of that review is kept?

openPoints.issue: No approval thresholds or delegation of authority were described for requisition approval.
openPoints.question: Do higher-value requisitions route to a more senior approver, and where is the delegation of authority documented?

openPoints.issue: It isn't stated what happens when the PO value check fails, or whether anyone can override it.
openPoints.question: When the PO value check fails, is the PO blocked outright, and who (if anyone) can override the block?

openPoints.issue: There's no owner or time limit described for following up parked invoices.
openPoints.question: Who monitors parked invoices, and how long can one stay parked before it's escalated?

openPoints.issue: The 'receiving team' was mapped into the Procurement lane; the walkthrough doesn't say where it sits.
openPoints.question: Is the receiving team part of Procurement, or a separate warehouse/stores function?
